transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, it’s probably not a huge thing, but I’ve been having a little trouble staying focused at work. I’m a receptionist, and lately I’ll be scheduling appointments or fixing up the lobby displays, and I sort of lose my place. My mind drifts to what I might’ve forgotten or overlooked, and then I have to backtrack. I just thought maybe I should ask about it before it becomes more of a problem… if that makes sense.
Do you find yourself worrying more than usual about things at work or in your daily life?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I try not to make too much of it, because everyone worries, right? But lately I do catch myself worrying about kind of ordinary things—work schedules, bills, travel plans, even little paperwork mistakes. It’s like my mind jumps to, “What if this small mix-up turns into something bigger?” I know that may sound a bit silly, but it’s been happening more than it used to.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually restless or on edge lately?

A little, yes. I mean, I can still do my job and be pleasant with people at the front desk, so it’s not like I’m falling apart or anything. But inside I do feel kind of wound tight sometimes… like my shoulders are up by my ears, and I’m sort of bracing for something to go wrong. Does that make sense?
Have you noticed yourself feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or time with family and friends?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I have normal off days, like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been feeling really sad or losing interest in people or things. I still enjoy seeing my family and doing my usual stuff when I can. I hope that’s the kind of thing you mean.
Have you noticed feeling fatigued or lacking energy more often than usual, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly tiring?

I’m not sure I’d say fatigued exactly. I mean, I get tired like anyone does after work or a busy day, but I haven’t really noticed a big lack of energy when I haven’t done much. Nothing that feels unusual, I don’t think. Does that answer it okay?
Do you find it hard to control or let go of your worries once they start?

Yes… sometimes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I can usually keep going, but once a worry starts it can be hard to just set it down. I’ll tell myself, “Sunny, it’s handled,” but then the thought keeps looping, and pretty soon I’ve jumped from that one concern to another. Then I’m checking details in my head over and over, like I’m trying to make sure I didn’t miss anything. Is that what you mean?
Have you had days where you felt down or blue, even when things were going okay, or found less pleasure in things that usually make you happy?

Not really, no. I mean, I have a day here and there where I’m a little off or tired of everything, but not like feeling blue when things are fine, and I still get pleasure from the things I usually like. I don’t think that’s been a problem for me. Is that okay?
Have you noticed any changes in your mood, like feeling down or losing enjoyment in specific situations that used to make you happy, even if just temporarily?

I don’t think so, not in a way that stands out. I mean, I can get briefly irritated or sort of worn out by certain situations, but I wouldn’t say I’m losing enjoyment in things that usually make me happy. It seems more like normal ups and downs to me… unless I’m missing what you mean?
Have you noticed that, in certain situations where you used to feel happy or satisfied, you now feel little or no pleasure, even if just for a short time?

No, I don’t think I’ve noticed that. If I’m in a situation I usually enjoy, I generally still feel good about it. Maybe I can be distracted sometimes, but I wouldn’t say the pleasure is gone or anything like that. I hope that makes sense.
Have you noticed any situations that usually make you feel good — even small things — where you now feel little or no happiness at all, even just for a moment?

Honestly, no… I don’t think so. I’m trying to think of little things too, like small enjoyable moments, and I can’t really come up with anything where I feel no happiness at all. Maybe I get distracted or preoccupied sometimes, but I still can enjoy things. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Have you noticed that in specific situations—like after finishing a task or spending time with someone you care about—you don’t feel the usual sense of satisfaction or happiness, even just for a little while?

No, I don’t think so. Like if I finish something, or I’m with someone I care about, I still feel that little bit of satisfaction or happiness. Maybe I’m not always totally focused on it, but I wouldn’t say it’s missing. I hope I’m answering that the right way.
Have you ever had a time when something upsetting happened, and you felt down or lost interest in things more than you normally would, even if just for a few days?

I’m not sure… I mean, upsetting things have happened, of course, but I don’t think I’ve had a time where I felt down or lost interest in things beyond what seems normal. Maybe I’d feel bothered for a bit, but not like I stopped caring about things for days. I hope that answers what you’re asking.

Can you think of any recent times when you were in a situation that usually makes you feel good—like spending time with a friend or enjoying a hobby—where you felt noticeably less pleasure or satisfaction than you normally would, even just for a short while?

I don’t think so… not in a noticeable way. Like, if I’m with a friend or doing something I usually like, I can still enjoy it. I might be a little in my head sometimes, but I wouldn’t say the pleasure or satisfaction is really reduced. I hope that makes sense.

Have you noticed that in the past few weeks, there’s been a drop in how much you enjoy things like spending time with friends, doing hobbies, or other activities you used to look forward to, even if just for a little while?

I don’t think I’ve noticed a real drop, no. I still look forward to seeing people or doing things I like. I might be distracted sometimes, but the enjoyment is still there, at least as far as I can tell. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like muscle tension, trouble sleeping, or feeling more tired than usual because of all this worrying?

A little, yes… I mean, I can still do my job and be pleasant at the front desk, so it’s not like I’m falling apart. But inside I do feel kind of wound tight sometimes, like my shoulders are up around my ears and I’m just waiting for something to go wrong. I don’t know if that counts as physical, but that’s what I notice.
Have you had trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because your mind is racing with worries?

Yes… I think so, a bit. Most nights I’ll get into bed feeling tired, but then my mind starts going over things for work, like tomorrow’s appointments or whether I forgot some form or message. I do fall asleep eventually, but it feels like I don’t really settle all the way, and I wake up feeling like I didn’t sleep as well as I should. I don’t know if that’s “trouble sleeping,” exactly, but it’s been happening.
